gaps: No evidence identifies applicable WCAG success criteria or distinguishes normative requirements from recommended web-platform practices.

Accessible tabs are unsupported: tablist/tab/tabpanel semantics, accessible names, selected state, relationships, keyboard navigation, activation behavior and focus management need primary-source coverage.
Visible focus is unsupported: keyboard operability, focus visibility, focus appearance and protection from focus obscuration need applicable WCAG guidance and implementation evidence.

Reduced-motion transitions are unsupported: user preference detection with prefers-reduced-motion, appropriate transition alternatives and relevant WCAG animation requirements need primary-source coverage.

Responsive web performance is unsupported: responsive layout and media delivery, loading and rendering practices, and performance measurement need primary-source coverage; their relationship to accessibility also remains unexplained.
